title: RRB JE CBT 1 science revision notes: formulas, SI units and worked checks
description: Revise mechanics, electricity, heat, chemistry and biology with concise notes, common traps and eight original worked checks for Railway CBT 1.
intro: Use these original revision notes alongside the science topics in your RRB syllabus. They are a compact recall aid for JE CBT 1 and also useful for basic-science revision by ALP or Group D candidates. They are not an official key, complete syllabus or prediction of questions. For JE CEN 04/2026, check the separately posted e-call-letter link before travel.

sections.title: Motion, force, work and units
sections.body:
Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18; reverse with 18/5. Average speed is total distance divided by total time. For equal distances travelled at speeds u and v, it is 2uv/(u+v), not generally their arithmetic mean.

Use F = ma, momentum p = mv, kinetic energy = ½mv² and power = work/time. For constant force parallel to motion, work = force × displacement. The SI units are newton for force, joule for energy/work and watt for power. Convert mass to kilograms before substituting. Speed is scalar; velocity includes direction. Zero instantaneous velocity does not necessarily mean zero acceleration.

sections.title: Electricity: identify series, parallel and rating
sections.body:
Ohm’s law gives V = IR for an ohmic conductor under fixed physical conditions. Series resistances add; for two parallel resistors, equivalent R = R₁R₂/(R₁+R₂). Power P = VI, and with Ohm’s law P = I²R = V²/R.

A kilowatt-hour is energy: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. It is not a power unit. For a rated appliance, the stated power corresponds to its rated operating conditions; do not reuse that power unchanged after a different voltage is applied without an appropriate model. Check whether a question asks for current, resistance, power or energy before choosing a formula.

sections.title: Heat and temperature: keep mass and scale consistent
sections.body:
For a temperature change without a phase transition, heat Q = mcΔT. During a phase change, use the latent-heat relation Q = mL where its assumptions apply. A one-degree Celsius temperature difference equals a one-kelvin difference, but absolute temperatures differ: kelvin = °C + 273.15.

Density = mass/volume; pressure = force/area. For 1 g/cm³, the SI density is 1000 kg/m³. Smaller area under the same force means greater pressure. In numerical questions, convert every input to a compatible unit before calculation rather than fixing units at the end.

sections.title: Chemistry and biology: use contrast pairs
sections.body:
For a neutral atom, protons equal electrons. Atomic number counts protons; mass number counts protons plus neutrons. Isotopes have the same atomic number and different mass numbers. Balance a chemical equation by changing coefficients, not by changing the substances’ chemical formulae.

At 25°C, neutral aqueous solutions have pH 7; acidic solutions are below 7 and basic solutions above 7. This familiar reference depends on temperature. In cells, mitochondria are associated with aerobic energy production, ribosomes with protein synthesis, and chloroplasts with photosynthesis in plants. Xylem transports water and minerals; phloem transports organic food substances. Test each pair in both directions instead of memorising only one prompt.

sections.title: Use the notes as a closed-book check
sections.body:
Read one section, close it and write the formulas with their units and one condition of use. Then attempt the original checks below. For each error, record whether the cause was recall, unit conversion, an unsuitable formula or arithmetic. Retry later with changed numbers.

The [JE final-revision guide](/exams/rrb-je/guides/cbt-1-final-revision-and-technical-bridge/) covers the wider study routine. The [JE admit-card update](/exam-updates/rrb-je-2026-cbt-1-e-call-letter/) links the official admission listing. ALP candidates should use their [own city-slip update](/exam-updates/rrb-alp-2026-city-intimation-cbt-1/) rather than the JE login.

drills.explanation: 72 × 5/18 = 20. The conversion comes from 1000 metres per kilometre and 3600 seconds per hour.

drills.prompt: Equal distances are travelled at 30 and 60 km/h. Find the average speed.
drills.explanation: Use 2 × 30 × 60/(30+60) = 40. More time is spent at the slower speed.

drills.prompt: A 2 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s². What net force acts on it?
drills.explanation: F = ma = 2 × 3. The result is a net force, not necessarily the value of each individual force.

drills.prompt: A 2 kg body moves at 4 m/s. Find its kinetic energy.
drills.explanation: ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 16 = 16. Square the speed before multiplying.

drills.prompt: A 12 V source is connected across an ideal 6 Ω resistor. Find current and power.
drills.explanation: I = V/R = 2 A; P = VI = 24 W. This is the ideal-resistor model.

drills.prompt: Two 6 Ω resistors are connected in parallel. Find their equivalent resistance.
drills.explanation: 6 × 6/(6+6) = 3. For two equal parallel resistors, the equivalent is half of either resistance.

drills.prompt: A 100 W appliance runs for 5 hours at its stated power. Find the electrical energy in kWh.
drills.explanation: 100 W = 0.1 kW; energy = power × time = 0.1 × 5 = 0.5 kWh.

drills.prompt: A neutral atom has atomic number 17 and mass number 35. How many protons, electrons and neutrons does it have?
drills.explanation: Protons = atomic number. Neutrality makes electrons equal protons. Neutrons = 35 − 17.

checklist: Write each formula with units and a condition of use.
Distinguish power from energy and speed from velocity.
Convert numerical inputs to compatible units before substitution.
Attempt the original checks without looking at answers.
Use the admission link for my own CEN and read my e-call letter.

faqs.q: Is this an official Railway answer key?
faqs.a: No. It is an original revision aid with original worked questions.

faqs.q: Can ALP and Group D candidates use it?
faqs.a: The underlying science can help revision, but compare it with your own CEN syllabus and paper structure. The JE admission link does not apply to another recruitment.
